# S-4 · Documentation of Planned Control Implementations

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Step | S Select (system level) |
| Phases | PH-TMRR (primary), PH-EMD |
| Depends on | S-3 |
| Inputs | ART-BASELINE, ART-SD, ART-BND, ART-INV, EXT-CATALOG |
| Outputs | ART-SSP (produces), ART-CMP (produces), ART-CP (produces), ART-IRP (produces), ART-SVCA (produces) |
| Writes facts | — |
| Minimum interviews | 1 |
| RACI | R: PER-ISSM, PER-CCP, PER-ISSE · A: PER-PM · C: PER-AO, PER-IO, PER-PRIV, PER-ISSO, PER-DEV, PER-CSSP, PER-CCB · I: — · PER-PRIV only when the system processes PII |

Purpose: Document the planned control implementations in the security plan and write the CM, contingency and incident response plans.
<!-- END rmf:header -->
<!-- rmf:body authored -->

## Steps

1. **Entry check.** S-3 is done, deferred or seeded: `artifacts/data/allocation.yaml` and
   `artifacts/data/tailoring.yaml` exist, and `baseline.json` is current (S-1 ran
   `rmf baseline resolve`). Why: each statement is written for an allocated control and its
   components, with the tailored parameter values.
2. **Read the inputs** in `## Inputs` once: the system description, boundary, inventory,
   tailoring and allocation. Keep the component IDs and parameter values at hand.
3. **Work family by family** with `_shared/ssp-batching.md` (gap list, catalog listing,
   batched interviews, whole-file write, build, family check, CHECKPOINT), at most 3
   families per session. For each control, write one record:
   - `control_id`: the OSCAL ID from the catalog listing (`ac-2`).
   - `status`, the honest state of the control **as planned and built today**:

     | Status | Use when |
     |---|---|
     | `implemented` | the system fully does what the control requires |
     | `partial` | part is in place; the statement says what is missing and the plan |
     | `planned` | nothing is in place yet; the statement gives the plan and date |
     | `alternative` | a different mechanism meets the intent; say which and why |
     | `not-applicable` | the control cannot apply; `rationale` is required |
     | `inherited` | a provider fully implements it; `inherited_from` is required |

     A known limitation in the product material (a shared account, a late patch cycle)
     makes a control `partial`, never `implemented`. Why: the assessor tests the
     statement; an overstated SSP becomes a finding and misleads the AO.
   - `statement`: how the system meets each part of the control on its components: who does
     what, with which mechanism, how often. Use the tailored parameter values from
     `tailoring.yaml` (for example the review frequency) in the text.
   - `responsible_roles`: the persona IDs who carry out the control (`PER-ISSO`, ...).
   - `components`: the components `allocation.yaml` lists for the control, exactly.
   - `inherited_from`: for `inherited`, and for a control `allocation.yaml` marks `hybrid`
     or `common`, the provider named in `allocation.yaml`; describe the system's own part in
     the statement.
   - `parameters`: `param_id: value` for each `parameter` action in `tailoring.yaml` for
     the control.
   - `sources`: the interview answers and product passages behind the statement.
   - Where it applies, the optional fields of SP 800-18r2 3.2: `planned_io` (inputs, data
     sources and outputs of a technical control), `technical_objectives`, `automation` (reliance
     on automation and its thresholds), `artifact_locations` (policy, procedure and artifact
     locations; reference operational procedures instead of copying them),
     `information_sources` and, on an inherited control, `inherited_risks`.
   - `assurance`, for each control `rmf catalog show --fields assurance` marks as contributing
     to assurance that the system implements: `addressed` (the developer and implementer
     activities and the evidence they produce) and `status` (`satisfied` once the control is
     implemented). An inherited control's provider addresses its assurance (SSE-003).
4. **Write `artifacts/ART-SSP.md`** from `templates/artifacts/ART-SSP.md` after the last
   family: the approach to control implementation, inheritance and shared responsibility
   (one paragraph per provider), and the open items (each `partial` or `planned` control
   with its plan), each section traced. Do not copy the statements into the Markdown and
   do not write facts; the family files are the one home of the statements, and `rmf build`
   fills the facts block. Write `artifacts/data/plan-reviews.yaml` from
   `templates/data/plan-reviews.yaml` with the organization-defined review `schedule`; M-4 logs
   the reviews and changes (RUN-ART-001 asks for the file with ART-SSP).
5. **Write the plans and their records.** Each plan is a Markdown file from its template and a
   record a rule can judge, both whole. The record holds the values; the Markdown says why:
   - Privacy plan (a system processing PII): whether `plan_structure.consolidation` keeps the
     plans together or separate, `ssp-records.yaml` `privacy_plan` gives an overview of the privacy requirements and the
     methodologies and metrics that assess the privacy controls (PRIV-008); ART-SSP
     `## Privacy plan` says why. Interview PER-PRIV on it.
   - ART-CMP: `artifacts/ART-CMP.md` and `artifacts/data/cm-plan.yaml`. Every inventory item
     sits in one and only one configuration item, and one CI holds the SecCM tools and testing
     processes (CMPL-001). A tool that is not SCAP-validated while a validated one exists is
     refused; `manual_monitoring` lists what tools cannot reach (CMPL-002).
   - ART-CP: `artifacts/ART-CP.md` and `artifacts/data/contingency.yaml`, every section of the
     template written. RTO plus reprocessing stays under the MTD, or `strategy.rto_gaps` names a
     POA&M item; an essential function keeps an MTD of 12 hours or less (CPLAN-001). The exercise
     depth follows the availability impact (CPLAN-002). One exercise runs under realistic cyber
     conditions and tests work-arounds and fall-backs, one tests loss of all information
     resources and connectivity, and `strategy.dynamic_allocation.proved_by` names the exercise
     that proved the allocation (CPLAN-003).
   - ART-IRP: `artifacts/ART-IRP.md` and `artifacts/data/incident-response.yaml`. A
     `reporting_paths` record for each case IRPT-001 and IRPT-002 name, with its authority and
     recipients. Mark `cleared-contractor-loss` `applies: false` with a rationale only when no
     cleared contractor system touches the program.
   - ART-SVCA: `artifacts/ART-SVCA.md` and `artifacts/data/service-agreements.yaml`, one record
     per provider, the CSSP first. A provider named in `inherited_from` in the family files uses
     the same `provider` string, so its controls are checked against the agreement (SVCA-001).
   - ART-SSP's records: `artifacts/data/ssp-records.yaml`: `funding` for implementation,
     assessment, sustainment, configuration and vulnerability management (FUND-001);
     `cryptography`, per use, with the approval (CRYP-001; CRYP-002 on a space NSS); `telework`
     (TELE-001); the E-Authentication answer; and the `plan_structure` decision.
   - Software: `artifacts/data/software.yaml` from `templates/data/software.yaml` (DoWI
     8430.01; SWA-001). `covered_software` is true for any software, firmware, operating
     system, application or cloud service developed, acquired, integrated or operated for the
     DoW; a hardware product that holds none says why in `covered_software_reason`. Covered
     software that is wholly acquired sets `pipeline.produced: false` with a `reason`; its SBOM
     still holds the COTS, third-party and transitive components.
   Set `space_nss: true` only for a system CNSSP 12 scopes in. On a space NSS, write the SKMP
   and each CSP in the format and information content NSA specifies, and record each in
   `cryptography.space` with its submission and NSA approval dates (CRYP-002). A system
   designated an NSS complies with CNSS policy issuances: CNSSI 1253 selects its baseline,
   CNSSP 15 governs its cryptography (CRYP-001), CNSSP 12 a space NSS (CRYP-002) and CNSSI
   1010 its incident reporting (IRPT-001); name any other CNSS issuance the product material
   invokes in `artifact_locations` of the control it shapes. Why: these are the values the
   assessor, the AO and a later rule read; a heading alone cannot be wrong.
6. **Build and check the task.** `uv run rmf build <run>`, then
   `uv run rmf check <run> --task S-4`, until 0 errors. SSP-COV-001 requires a statement for
   every control in `baseline.json`.
7. **Journal** a CHECKPOINT for the task (family CHECKPOINTs were written in step 3).

## Interviews

| Persona | Why | Question focus |
|---|---|---|
| PER-ISSO | consulted (C); runs accounts, logging and patching | account lifecycle and reviews, events logged and who reviews them, patch cadence, evidence kept |
| PER-ISSE | responsible (R); designed the controls | boundary protection, configuration baseline, authentication design, how each allocated component implements its part |
| PER-DEV | consulted (C); built it | hardening in the build, update bundles, what the code enforces (lockout, session lock) |
| PER-CCP | responsible (R) for inherited parts | what the provider implements, what the system must configure or report, evidence of the provider's authorization |
| PER-CSSP | consulted (C); provides cybersecurity services | the agreement, services, controls, sensors, evaluation, and the reporting paths and timelines |
| PER-PM | accountable (A); funds the plan | the budget lines, what is unfunded, the recovery budget |

At least 1 interview; batch by family (`_shared/ssp-batching.md` step 3). In the skeleton
scenario one interview per persona can cover all 6 controls.

- `baseline.json` (generated; the controls to cover)
- `artifacts/data/tailoring.yaml`, `artifacts/data/allocation.yaml`, `artifacts/ART-BASELINE.md`
- `artifacts/ART-SD.md`, `artifacts/data/users.yaml`
- `artifacts/ART-BND.md`, `artifacts/data/boundary.yaml`
- `artifacts/ART-INV.md`, `artifacts/data/inventory.yaml`

- `product/architecture.md`, `product/conops.md`

## Facts

S-4 writes no facts.

## Done when

- Every control in `baseline.json` has exactly one statement (SSP-COV-001, SSP-DUP-001), and
  every `not-applicable` or `inherited` statement has its rationale or provider
  (SSP-STAT-001).
- ART-SSP, ART-CMP, ART-CP, ART-IRP and ART-SVCA exist with S-4 in `touched_by`, with their
  records, `artifacts/data/software.yaml` among them (SWA-001), and each implemented
  assurance-related control carries its `assurance` (SSE-003).
- ART-CMP, ART-CP and ART-IRP keep every heading their templates name, each written and
  traced; a later task adds its sections after them (TPL-001).
- `uv run rmf check <run> --task S-4` reports 0 errors.

## Journal and lessons

- One CHECKPOINT per family: `## <time> · CHECKPOINT · task S-4 · family: <fam>`.
- A final CHECKPOINT for the task: `## <time> · CHECKPOINT · task S-4`, with the status mix
  (implemented / partial / planned / inherited / n/a).
- A family file rewritten after a failed check is a RETRY with a lesson
  (`_shared/journaling-and-lessons.md`).
